units.headline: Job matching now trims slashes and ignores case
units.summary: The new comparison matches running jobs to sidebar results and highlights them, ignoring trailing slashes and letter case. Its treatment of local paths affects whether a reviewer sees a running triage log or an existing result.
focus: Relative or symlinked local paths against the absolute path stored in results
Distinct local repositories whose paths differ only by case

issues.title: Relative paths fail to match running local jobs
issues.detail: The server keeps the path entered by the user as the job URL, while local results store a resolved absolute path. This comparison does not reconcile those forms, so opening an existing result during retriage shows the old result instead of the running job.
issues.failure_scenario: A result stores /work/repo. The user starts retriage with ./repo from /work; the job URL is ./repo. Clicking the result does not find that job and opens the old result.

issues.title: Case folding conflates distinct local repositories
issues.detail: Lowercasing local paths treats distinct repositories as the same on a case-sensitive filesystem. The sidebar can mark the wrong result as triaging and open another repository's job log.
issues.failure_scenario: On a case-sensitive filesystem, /work/Repo and /work/repo are separate repositories. With a job running for /work/Repo, clicking the existing result for /work/repo opens that job log.

units.headline: Mark sidebar results with running triage jobs

issues.title: Local triage marks other branches as running
issues.detail: Local results are listed separately by path and branch, but this function matches them by path alone. A triage of one branch marks every saved branch result from that path as running.
issues.failure_scenario: Save results for branches A and B from the same local checkout, then start triaging branch B. Both sidebar rows show the pulsing triage indicator, although only B is being triaged.

units.headline: Job polling highlights matching results in the sidebar
units.summary: The job watcher now updates the sidebar's active result on each poll by comparing its source with the job URL. This keeps a matching result highlighted while its job runs, but the comparison loses that highlight for some local jobs.
focus: Sidebar selection during local triage started with a relative or `~/` path
Sidebar selection while fixing a local result
Selection after a job finishes or fails

issues.title: Local jobs clear their result's active highlight
issues.detail: The match uses the job's raw URL, but local triage jobs can retain a relative or `~/` path while sidebar results use an absolute path. Local fix jobs also have an empty URL when the result has no PR link. In both cases, polling removes the active highlight from the associated result.
issues.failure_scenario: A saved local result has `data-src="/home/user/repo"`. Starting triage with `~/repo`, or starting a fix for that result when it has no PR URL, makes `same(...)` false and clears its active sidebar row while the job runs.

units.headline: Job refresh marks sidebar results with running triage jobs

issues.title: Relative local paths hide active retriage
issues.detail: Local jobs retain the path entered in the form, while saved results use a resolved absolute path. The new marker update cannot match those values for relative or symlinked paths, so the sidebar does not show that an existing result is being retriaged.
issues.failure_scenario: An existing result has local_path `/work/repo`; the user starts another triage with `./repo`. The running job's URL is `./repo`, so the existing sidebar item never gets the triaging marker, and selecting it opens the old result instead of the running job.

issues.title: Local path aliases fail to match running jobs
issues.detail: Local results store a canonical absolute path, while a running job keeps the path entered by the user. Retriaging through a relative or symlinked path leaves the existing result unmarked, and selecting it opens the old result instead of the running job.

overview.why: Inferred from the changes: reviewers need to see when a saved result is being triaged again and follow the replacement job instead of reading an older review.
how: Pass each saved result’s PR URL or local path through sidebar selection and store it on the sidebar row.
Track running triage jobs, mark matching sidebar results with a pulsing indicator, and restore markers after refreshes.
Open the live job log when a saved result matches a running triage, then open the new result when the job finishes.
issues: Local jobs started with relative, `~/`, or symlinked paths can miss saved results, leaving them unmarked and opening the old review instead of the live log.
Case insensitive path matching can mark a different repository and open its job log on case sensitive filesystems.
Triaging one branch of a local repository marks saved results for other branches at the same path.
Polling can clear the active sidebar highlight for local fix jobs whose job URL is empty.
